Subject: Dedicated sizing intake for BrightRetail — initial info

Hi Vanessa,

Thanks for taking this — we'd like to start the conversation around a dedicated deployment for BrightRetail. High level context below; happy to jump on a call to walk through details.

High level workload
- Use case: conversational search + product Q&A (user-facing, low-latency), occasional long-form generation for marketing templates.
- Expected active users: 1.2M monthly active, ~120k daily active during promotions.

Traffic patterns
- Baseline concurrent requests (steady-state): ~120 concurrent inference requests
- Peak seasonal bursts: up to ~3,000 concurrent at peak (Black Friday style bursts, <8 hours)
- Average requests/sec (day): 180 QPS steady, peaks to 2,800 QPS during flash campaigns

Model/profile
- Prefer using open weights (we plan to use a quantized Llama-family model) — target 16–32k context in some prompts.
- Typical prompt length: 40–80 tokens; typical response length: 120–300 tokens. For search queries it's much shorter (~15 tokens).

SLOs and latency
- P95 latency target: <= 250 ms for chat/search paths; can tolerate up to 600 ms for long-form generations.
- Hard SLA: availability 99.9% for production routes.

Other constraints
- Must run in a VPC/private deployment.
- Data residency: US only.
- Will want audit logs and token-level cost visibility.

Can you send a sizing questionnaire or a short template we can fill? Also, what initial fleet profiles should we consider (A100 vs H100, counts, autoscale buffers) given the numbers above?

Thanks,
Lauren Meyer\Director, AI Platforms\BrightRetail

Quick first-pass sizing notes (two options):

Performance-first (low latency, more capacity headroom):
- Fleet: 6 x H100-80GB (pinned) + autoscale pool to add 6 more during promos (total 12)
- Effective concurrency: ~45 inference streams per H100 for chat/search mix (with optimized kernels and int8 quantized 33B variant using KV cache)
- Expected P95: ~140–180 ms for short search; ~350–500 ms for long-form depending on batching
- Notes: H100 keeps memory headroom for 16k context and simplifies model sharding for 33B.

Cost-conscious (balanced):
- Fleet: 8 x A100-80GB (pinned) + autoscale to 12 for peaks
- Effective concurrency: ~30–40 per A100 depending on batching; better price/$ but higher tail latency for long-context routes
- Suggest int8 quant for 13B, consider mixed int8/int4 for 33B in lower-SLA routes

Operational suggestions:
- Enable prefix KV caching for product search queries (estimated 40% cache hit from prompt similarity) to reduce per-token compute and lower tail latency.
- Use per-route model pinning: 13B quantized for search, 33B quantized for high-quality generation routes.
- Autoscale policy: target CPU/GPU utilization thresholds and queue-length triggers; pre-warm extra GPUs 1h before scheduled promos.

I'll draft a short summary to send to Lauren post-call.

-Marco

Hi Lauren — thanks again for the worksheet and for joining the call this morning. Per our discussion, here is the first-pass sizing and next steps. Attaching a one-page summary (brightretail_sizing_summary.pdf).

First-pass recommendation (performance-first)
- Initial pinned fleet: 6 x H100-80GB GPUs in a VPC private deployment
- Autoscale buffer: add up to +6 GPUs automatically for marketing events (pre-warm 1 hour prior to campaign windows)
- Model split: quantized 13B for search routes (int8), quantized 33B for generation routes (int8 default; consider int4 on non-critical routes after QA)
- Expected effective concurrency: ~40–45 streams per H100 for mixed traffic; should meet P95 <= 250ms for short search paths
- Long-context jobs (16k): schedule to dedicated batch workers or isolate to separate route to avoid impacting search latency

Cost-conscious alternative
- 8 x A100-80GB pinned, autoscale to 12 for peaks; tradeoff is higher long-tail latency for 16k workloads but lower unit GPU cost in some clouds

Operational items / next steps
- Procurement: Lauren / BrightRetail to share vendor contact for cloud region and any onboarding security docs.
- Redwood action: provide formal capacity proposal & pricing (est. 2 business days) and SOC-2 evidence for Private deployment.
- HubSpot: I'll attach the summary and link to the deal (BR-8421) for your procurement team.

Attachments: brightretail_sizing_summary.pdf
Related link: https://app.hubspot.com/deal/BR-8421

If this looks good I can convert to a formal Dedicated Capacity proposal and include RU/price schedules.
